3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: The angelic-sounding voices of a boys' choir echoed through the Great Hall of Palas Rezna.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: To most Rizians, this was the grandest room in the grandest building in the entire country. To me, it was just home.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: I remembered playing hide-and-seek among the mosaic-tiled columns while visiting my grandmother. Goofing off with Pabel in the upper gallery as my father met with foreign dignitaries.

9.speaker: Narrator
9.text: I remembered playing hide-and-seek among the mosaic-tiled columns while visiting my grandmother. Watching from the upper gallery as my father met with foreign dignitaries.

10.speaker: Narrator
10.text: And of course, this was where I had married Lena...

11.speaker: Narrator
11.text: The hall before me was filled with nobles, politicians, business magnates, even movie stars. A television crew moved up and down the aisles, broadcasting the ceremony to the Rizian public for the first time.

12.speaker: Narrator
12.text: My mother was sitting in the front row next to Uncle Hugo.

13.speaker: Narrator
13.text: Tradition dictated that in the absence of a king or queen consort, the seat next to me would be filled by the successor to the throne. Vina plucked at a stray thread in her gown.

16.speaker: Player_Romus
16.text: "My feelings are none of your business."

17.speaker: Player_Romus
17.text: "Shh. Stop fidgeting. The cameras are on us."

19.speaker: Narrator
19.text: The final notes of the coronation hymn "By His Sword I Live" rang out. An expectant silence filled the hall.

20.speaker: Narrator
20.text: It was broken by the sound of shuffling footsteps. The cameras followed Grand Wiseman Sal Ignacius as he walked slowly down the central aisle, bearing a velvet cushion.

21.speaker: Narrator
21.text: He presented it in front of me. On it was the Toras crown, a black onyx orb and a scroll containing the words to the royal oath.

22.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic

28.speaker: Player_Romus
28.text: "I promise to guide my country with a steadfast hand."

29.speaker: Player_Romus
29.text: "To uphold the laws of this land under St. Wruhec's watchful eye."

30.speaker: Player_Romus
30.text: "To wield the sword of justice and the shield of mercy in equal measure."

31.speaker: Player_Romus
31.text: "All this I shall do until the day I die."

33.speaker: Narrator
33.text: With trembling hands, Grand Wiseman Ignacius lifted the crown off the cushion.

46.speaker: Narrator
46.text: I could spot a grey hair still clinging to its inner rim. My father's.

47.speaker: Narrator
47.text: The crown came down on my head. Its heaviness surprised me.

49.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
49.text: Break tradition and make a speech first.

50.speaker: Narrator
50.text: I hoped my limp wasn't visible to television viewers. I thought about the kidnapper's bullet and how close I had come to never seeing this day.

51.speaker: Narrator
51.text: We reached the end of the hall, where a spiral staircase led to the palace balcony.

52.speaker: Player_Romus
52.text: "I've got to do this part alone."

53.speaker: Player_Romus
53.text: "Come, Vina, let's greet your future subjects."

54.speaker: Player_Romus
54.text: "I know this is highly unusual, but we are living in unusual times."

56.speaker: Narrator
56.text: Uncle Hugo had been smiling proudly up to this point. His expression now grew serious.

57.speaker: Player_Romus
57.text: "When my father died, I made a promise. One that I would like to share with you all today."

58.speaker: Player_Romus
58.text: "My father was a great but flawed man. His mistakes will not be repeated."

59.speaker: Player_Romus
59.text: "The reign of Valero Toras is over. A new day has dawned."

60.speaker: Player_Romus
60.text: "Under my rule, Rizia will be transformed."

61.speaker: Player_Romus
61.text: "I will succeed where our previous king failed."

62.speaker: Player_Romus
62.text: "It is time to show all of Merkopa what Rizia is capable of."

63.speaker: Player_Romus
63.text: "We must break with tradition and enter the 20th century."

64.speaker: Player_Romus
64.text: "I will uphold the monarchy and restore the glory days of House Toras."

65.speaker: Player_Romus
65.text: "I promise I will take back the lands that have been stolen from us."

68.speaker: Player_Romus
68.text: "Only when Rizia is once again whole can a new era of peace and prosperity begin."

69.speaker: Player_Romus
69.text: "Only by achieving harmony with our neighbors can a new era begin."

70.speaker: Player_Romus
70.text: "Only once Rizia is united under a strong king can a new era begin."

75.speaker: Narrator
75.text: The hall fell silent again. My uncle was the first to speak.

77.speaker: Narrator
77.text: The attendees hurriedly broke into enthusiastic applause. The choir restarted the national anthem.

79.speaker: Narrator
79.text: My daughter beamed and put her arm through mine. We walked up and up the stairs until we came to a door.

80.speaker: Narrator
80.text: Leaving Vina behind, I walked up and up the stairs until I came to a door.

82.speaker: Narrator
82.text: When my eyes adjusted, I regarded the scene below me. Thousands and thousands of people were packed onto the palace grounds, some waving the Rizian flag, others the House Toras banner.

83.speaker: Narrator
83.text: Just beyond them, at the gates, the police easily held back a small pocket of protesters.

84.speaker: Narrator
84.text: I paid little attention to them. I was focused on the noise of the crowd, an overwhelming roar that gradually cohered into a single chant: "Salutenas axa regu novus!"

86.speaker: Player_Romus
86.text: "We must stop letting our past grudges dictate our future."

87.speaker: Narrator
87.text: I sat upright in the Sila Orica, the gold-plated wooden throne on which all monarchs of Rizia were coronated.

90.speaker: Sal Ignacius
90.text: "May St. Wruhec fill you with his holy spirit on this day, as he did your ancestors before you."
90.conditionsRaw: Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Coronation_RecitedOath"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Coronation_TookOrb"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Coronation_LookedAtCrown"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Coronation_LookedEstela"] == true

93.speaker: Sal Ignacius
93.text: "May you keep the promises you have made before God and your people."

94.speaker: Sal Ignacius
94.text: "By the divine power vested in me, I proclaim you sovereign king of Rizia."

100.speaker: Narrator
100.text: Uncle Hugo had been smiling politely up to this point. His expression now grew serious.

104.speaker: Narrator
104.text: I remembered wandering between the mosaic-tiled columns as a bored teenager. Goofing off with Pabel in the upper gallery as my father met with foreign dignitaries.

108.speaker: Narrator
108.text: I remembered wandering between the mosaic-tiled columns as a bored teenager. Watching from the upper gallery as my father met with foreign dignitaries.

113.speaker: Player_Romus
113.text: "Only when the people of Rizia are given a voice can a new era begin."

117.speaker: Vina Toras
117.text: "Me, too. I wish Mother was the one sitting here, though."

120.speaker: Narrator
120.text: My daughter sat up straight and folded her hands in her lap.

121.speaker: Narrator
121.text: My daughter seemed to shrink in her chair.

126.speaker: Narrator
126.text: The ceremonial robes I was wearing chafed against the scar on my shoulder. I thought about the kidnapper's bullet and how close I had come to never seeing this day.

166.speaker: Narrator
166.text: It was made of pure gold, adorned with two twisting spires resembling bull's horns.

167.speaker: Narrator
167.text: It was inlaid with a trio of diamonds, representing the three royal houses of Rizia: Toras, Azaro and Sazon.

171.speaker: Player_Romus
171.text: "May God bless this country and its people."

172.speaker: Narrator
172.text: Glory to Rizia. His shout reverberated throughout the hall.

174.speaker: Narrator
174.text: Everyone in the crowd bowed their heads as Vina and I made our way down the aisle.

175.speaker: Narrator
175.text: I passed my cousin Rico in the second row. He looked up at me and smiled.

179.speaker: Narrator
179.text: I passed my cousin Rico in the second row. He kept his head down and didn't acknowledge me.

180.speaker: Narrator
180.text: The entire back row was reserved for the Rumburgian royal family and their entourage. I could feel my sister-in-law Beatrice's eyes on me.

181.speaker: Narrator
181.text: As we kept walking, I recognized various other members of Rizia's three royal houses as well as monarchs from distant kingdoms.

184.speaker: Narrator
184.text: According to royal tradition, this was my signal to march down the aisle and up to the palace balcony to greet the public.
